audit.report: The checkout flow degraded after a batch_worker process (pid 1661119) entered an idle transaction holding locks, blocking 12 sessions. The business tolerated at most 60 seconds of checkout failure, but the blocker's expected remaining runtime was ~892 seconds, putting approximately $60,526/min of revenue at risk. After three rounds of negotiation, the Database Guardian recommended waiting for the blocker to complete, while the Continuity Guardian rejected each proposal because the wait time exceeded the 60-second degradation tolerance. The negotiation was escalated to inventory-platform with no agreement reached within three rounds (36.3 seconds total).
audit.root_cause: A batch_worker transaction became idle in lock, blocking checkout sessions beyond the 60-second business tolerance window.
lessons: Validate replay cost and idempotency early: batch_replayable_inventory is interruptible with a 4-minute replay cost, but this cost was not weighed against the 60-second revenue-at-risk ceiling until after three negotiation rounds.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly cited the 60-second tolerance and the 4-minute replay cost, but they deadlocked because neither provided evidence to override the I7 invariant that waiting exceeding 60s is unacceptable. The Database Guardian prioritized zero data loss, while the Continuity Guardian prioritized revenue-at-risk, resulting in three rounds without resolution.
follow_ups: Add a lock-wait threshold alert that triggers escalation when blocked sessions exceed 60 seconds of checkout degradation.
Pre-compute and cache the replay cost vs. revenue-at-risk trade-off for batch_replayable_inventory so the negotiation engine can compare them in round 1.
Confirm with inventory-platform whether the 4-minute replay can be split or parallelized to reduce the cost below the 60-second tolerance threshold.
